help.title: Your WordPress. Your settings.
help.text: Set up WordPress to suit your website. Clear options and prepared presets make configuration easier. You decide which settings apply and which features are active. Review a preset before applying it, save your choices and reuse proven configurations through import and export.

help.title: Bring your existing settings along.
help.text: Already using Unbloater, Falcon or both? The guided one-time takeover previews matching settings and highlights conflicts before you confirm changes. Configuration recovery remains available until a later settings save replaces the previous snapshot. You deactivate and remove the old plugins yourself. Guided settings takeover is provided specifically for Falcon and Unbloater.

help.title: Administration your clients can work with.
help.text: Hide rarely needed areas and make important settings easier to understand. Control access to menus, widgets and the Customizer by role, with local exceptions for individual users. These personal exceptions stay on the website and are excluded from exports.

help.title: Maintenance with your own WordPress page.
help.text: Design your maintenance page in the configured Block or Classic Editor. Visitors receive the maintenance page with HTTP 503 while administrators retain access. Preview the page before enabling maintenance; an orange toolbar indicator reminds administrators when it is active. Active Bricks, Elementor and Breakdance maintenance modes take precedence. Full-page caches may need to be cleared or bypassed.

help.title: Local avatars instead of external Gravatar requests.
help.text: Use your own user images from the Media Library. When enabled, the local avatar module prevents Gravatar requests for avatar output. Optionally show the images in the user table. If a supported provider already supplies local avatars, Site Essentials hides and pauses its own avatar module.

help.title: Keep important website settings in view.
help.text: Get administrator reminders when search indexing is discouraged, and confirm an intentional decision. Also check for missing, unpublished or detectably empty privacy and imprint pages. These checks do not assess legal compliance or the quality of legal text.

help.title: Several tasks. One shared place.
help.text: Depending on the functions you need, Site Essentials can replace additional individual plugins:

rows: Disable Comments or similar plugins
Disable comments completely or restrict them selectively
One User Avatar or similar plugins
Use local user images and prevent Gravatar requests
Page Links To
Set alternative post destinations; selectively copy existing Page Links To targets
Simple maintenance-mode plugins
Use your own WordPress page as a maintenance page

help.footnote: This does not promise full feature parity. Guided settings takeover applies specifically to Falcon and Unbloater. Page Links To target copying is separate; data from other plugins is not automatically migrated.

help.title: Getting started
help.text: Choose a preset or adjust individual settings, then save all settings. Preset and import previews do not change the site.

help.title: Multisite
help.text: Each site keeps its own configuration. The network can require the login language selector to be hidden. Local values remain stored.

help.title: Stored data
help.text: Deactivation and uninstall retain local settings, custom presets, one previous configuration and the network policy. No content is deleted.

help.title: Recovery
help.text: Restore the previous configuration, apply WordPress defaults, or deactivate the plugin to stop its runtime changes.

help.title: Replacing Falcon and Unbloater
help.text: Open Import and export to review Falcon 2.12.0 and Unbloater 1.7.0. Choose each source explicitly; current values, conflicts, differences and active functions without takeover are shown. Only confirmed local settings change. Source plugins and network policy remain untouched. The existing previous-configuration snapshot allows restoration until a later settings save replaces it.

help.title: Maintenance modes
help.text: Maintenance uses a published, non-password-protected WordPress page with its configured Classic or Block Editor. Save maintenance separately; activation and page selection never travel with presets or configuration recovery. Active Bricks, Elementor or Breakdance modes pause the own response until explicitly enabled again. APIs and webhooks remain accessible. Clear or bypass full-page caches and verify while signed out.

help.title: Testing missing pages and empty searches
help.text: Administrator-only links open a random missing address and an unusual search term in new tabs. They leave routing and content unchanged. Test while signed out as well; redirects, maintenance, search restrictions and caches may change the result. Theme-specific guidance explains where to review the views. These are manual checks, not automatic HTTP or template assessments.

help.title: Public resources and homepage response
help.text: Open robots.txt, the enabled native sitemap and feed addresses without changing the website. The manual administrator check retrieves the homepage and host-root robots.txt anonymously, with bounded requests and no cross-host redirect following. It displays HTTP status, redirect targets, content type, robots headers and HTML robots/canonical values, plus sitemap addresses listed in robots.txt. Results are observations, not a guarantee of indexability. No scheduled checks, external auditing service or stored report is used.

help.title: Maintenance, not Coming Soon
help.text: Site Essentials is designed for brief maintenance on an existing website. Its maintenance response uses HTTP 503 (temporarily unavailable) with Retry-After. This is not a Coming Soon mode for a launch page that should remain publicly available over a longer period. A public launch page normally uses HTTP 200; its indexing and access settings need separate decisions. Site Essentials does not offer a Coming Soon mode or a status-code switch. For a launch page, use a suitable theme, builder or dedicated plugin. A launch-page workflow is outside the scope of this focused maintenance tool.

help.title: Website addresses at a glance
help.text: Read the effective public site address and the address of the WordPress installation files under Website checks. Both values can be copied without editing settings. They can differ when WordPress is installed in a subdirectory. The Site Health link follows the native permission check.

help.title: Everyday checks and safeguards
help.text: Maintenance shows its activation time when recorded, using the website time zone. Existing activations without a recorded time are explicitly marked. A normal save retains the time; disabling clears it and explicitly resuming after a provider pause starts a new period. Public checks show when they ran and distinguish failed requests from missing declarations or uninspected HTML. Their compact copyable summary omits remote bodies and URL query strings. Save or discard unsaved configuration changes before separate maintenance or public-check actions.

help.title: Command palette and Site Health
help.text: Where WordPress already loads its command palette, administrators can open Site Essentials settings, reports and handover, website checks and maintenance mode. These commands only navigate; they do not apply presets, switch maintenance or run public requests. Site Health Info reports local maintenance state, a recorded activation time, page availability, detected maintenance providers and known overridden rules. No page titles, personal exceptions or public response contents are included. Public checks remain manual and their results are not retained.

help.title: Menus, without rebuilding them.
help.text: Enable menu duplication under Admin interface. The copy keeps native link properties, hierarchy and Site Essentials visibility, but receives no menu location. Third-party metadata is not copied. Visibility choices apply only to classic menus and do not protect target pages. Hidden parents also hide their descendants; page caches must distinguish login status.

help.title: User information, kept small.
help.text: User and content IDs offer a copy button with selectable-text fallback. Optional last-login collection stores only one successful interactive-login timestamp per user and website. Existing sessions do not update it. No IP address or history is stored. Only administrators with user-list permission see timestamps. WordPress personal-data tools can export and erase them; disabling collection retains existing timestamps, uninstall removes them.

help.title: Media trash: inspect before changing configuration.
help.text: The optional status card reads MEDIA_TRASH and EMPTY_TRASH_DAYS without editing wp-config.php. Enable native media trash only through server configuration before WordPress loads, respecting existing definitions and retention. A zero retention disables trash. Files in trash remain stored and may remain directly accessible; this is not a backup or privacy barrier. Explicit permanent deletion can bypass trash. On Multisite, constants normally apply across the installation.

help.title: Storage diagnosis without a live scan.
help.text: Enable daily local upload-storage diagnosis under Media library and view the cached result in Tools → System information and storage. Requests never scan directories while displaying the result. Measurements stop at 10,000 entries, 512 directories or two seconds. An incomplete or unavailable result is labeled without a partial total. Manual refresh queues a task, limited to fifteen-minute intervals. Traffic-dependent WordPress cron may run late. Remote media, the database and hosting quota are not measured.

help.title: One environment indicator.
help.text: Site Essentials uses the WordPress environment without changing it. When an active Brand Admin Schemes implementation provides its environment callback, BAS owns presentation and Site Essentials pauses, even if BAS hides its own badge. Site Essentials keeps its choice and resumes after BAS deactivation. The settings status explains which provider is responsible. No BAS files or settings are changed.

help.title: Feed references and readable feeds.
help.text: Choose which automatic feed discovery links are hidden in the page source. Blog, comment, category/tag, author and search references can be selected separately, plus registered content-type and taxonomy archives. Actual RSS/Atom feed access is unchanged; disabling feeds is a separate option. Existing broad suppression is retained, including future archives.

help.title: Successful update emails.
help.text: Suppress success notifications separately for WordPress, plugins and themes. Failure notifications are not suppressed by these controls. Existing broad suppression is retained for all three choices until you change them.

help.title: Find settings that are not applied.
help.text: Click the unapplied-rule count in the overview to see the affected settings, their known reasons and direct setting shortcuts. The shortcut clears any search so matching rules are not hidden. This changes the view only.

help.title: Media and list conveniences.
help.text: Optionally inspect generated image sizes in the attachment editor without changing files. New upload filenames can be converted to lowercase; existing files stay unchanged. Native content lists can offer a visible title-only search choice, with full search as the default. Featured-image, modified-date and administrator-only user-registration columns can be enabled separately. All four helpers start off.

help.title: Clear status, minimal diagnostics.
help.text: Known reasons for paused settings are shared across the rule overview, handover and Site Health. Support diagnostics use a reviewed allowlist: custom text, personal assignments and custom role or content-type names are omitted; lists disclose counts only. Storage diagnosis distinguishes no measurement, an incomplete measurement and an unavailable result.

help.title: One dashboard information widget.
help.text: Under Dashboard, configure one optional dashboard widget with a title, simple formatted text and an audience of roles plus additional site users. A matching role OR a selected user grants visibility; an empty audience grants nobody access. Users can hide it in Screen Options. Save this widget separately. Generic configuration and preset exports never include its text or personal grants. A separate, explicitly confirmed text export/import transfers only the saved title and text; it never transfers activation or audience. Disabling or uninstalling preserves the local configuration; resetting Site Essentials clears it.

help.title: A local default avatar.
help.text: Enable local avatars first. The optional user-list column and a separate default-image card then appear below the master setting. The card previews the current default and offers local media selection, raster upload or return to the shipped SE image. Save the image separately. A missing, deleted, private or externally served selection falls back to the shipped image. No media files are copied, locked or deleted when resetting the selection. Personal profile images still take priority. Image IDs are local to each website and are excluded from configuration, preset and support exports.

help.title: States and shortcuts without customer data.
help.text: Site Health Info reports whether the dashboard widget is enabled and whether a default avatar is supplied by SE, a local selection or a developer filter. It never includes widget text, contact details, selected users or image IDs/URLs. Administrator command-palette entries open dashboard information and, while SE local avatars are enabled, the default-avatar settings. These commands navigate only; they do not save or activate anything.

help.title: Default-avatar developer filter.
help.text: Developer filter: site_essentials_local_avatar_default_id returns a positive integer attachment ID from the current site, or 0 for no override. Only an available, public, locally served raster image is accepted. A valid override takes priority over the saved selection; otherwise the saved image and shipped SE image are used in that order. The UI explains a valid override and pauses selection without removing the saved value. Personal images remain first; force-default requests use the effective default.

help.title: Date and time, with clear examples.
help.text: Enable date and time explanations under Admin interface, then open WordPress General settings. Fixed examples explain leading zeros without changing formats, previews or saving. A Favicon and Home Screen explanation accompanies the native Site Icon controls.

en.about: Your WordPress. Your settings. Site Essentials brings focused settings and practical tools together for a WordPress website that fits your needs. Simplify administration, control WordPress features and reuse proven configurations across websites. Built for everyday site care and client handover, with support for single installations and individual sites in a Multisite network.
